Can’t believe there are still ppl who think crochet clothes look ugly when I think they’re some of the most beautiful pieces ever 😤 The fact that they can’t be made by machines makes each crochet piece feel so much more soulful and special! 🥹 If you’re trying to level up ur crochet game, here are some of my tips: 1. Opt for smaller yarn sizes! I started with size 4 Aran yarn, and now I literally never touch anything thicker than DK 🫢 Thicker yarn creates bulkier pieces! 2. Experiment with different fibers & ditch those milk cotton yarns 😩 Not trying to be a hater, but my milk cotton clothes are all too hot and stiff 🫠 Try plant-fiber yarns for a more airy result, or acrylic blends for something lighter! 3. Practice, practice, practice! Tension and hook choices matter too, so keep experimenting until you find what works for you~ What do you think? Do you also think crochet clothes look ugly? 🤔 Patterns featured: YVONNE, LUNA & HUĀ by me! 🤍 Use code YVONNE25 for 25% off all patterns until August 16! Mesh Hood Upcycle Tutorial 🧶 ... Details: • Weight 4 Acrylic Yarn, 4.5mm Hook • Running Stitch spacing is approximate but we do want these a little tighter than the usual half inch. • Ch4 counts as a TC. Ch6 counts as TC+Ch2. • Row 1 says 2TC in each, but you can add more. Total amount should be a multiple of 3, plus 1. The more stitches you have in R1, the broader your hood will be. • Use your judgment on this and also how many rows to do, every neck opening is a different size and so is every human head 😁 so you may have to adjust a little in that aspect. • Dec Rows can be adjusted as well, just keep the decs as centered as possible to create the curve. • Feel free to slip stitch or sew the sides together instead of single crochet. • Let me know if you have any questions! ... #crochet #crochettutorial #crochethood #howto #upcycle
